text: The plan from last lesson is clean. This final lesson applies it, reviews what actually got created, tears it down responsibly, and covers how to talk about this project when you're showing it to someone else.

Running apply creates all twelve resources, matching the plan exactly — no surprises, because the plan already told you what would happen. The outputs block at the end hands off the practical values, like the storefront's URL, without anyone having to dig through a console.

A dev environment that exists only to prove the pattern works doesn't need to run forever. Terraform destroy reads the same state file it used to build the environment, so it knows exactly what to remove and in what order — the reverse of the dependency graph from the very first chapter.

When you talk about this project afterward, lead with the decisions, not the tool — why directory-per-environment over workspaces, why tags were centralized in one place, what you'd add with more time. A real repo with a short README turns this from "I took a course" into something someone else can actually open and read.

You now have an end-to-end understanding of Terraform — HCL, state, modules, and running it safely as a team across both Azure and AWS. Congratulations on finishing Infrastructure as Code with Terraform. You're ready for what's next in the DevOps Engineer path.
